note: Real gap, but not fixable at the front-matter layer: tables in this book are NOT LaTeX floats (grep '\begin{table}' in render/latex/chapters/*.tex = 0). They are 76 labelled longtables, and 36 of the 76 '\label{tab:N.M}' entries have no retrievable title anywhere in the generated source (e.g. Table 27-1..27-4, 24-2..24-5, 16-3..16-6 appear only as \label inside a longtable, with no caption, heading, or in-text 'Table N-M' reference). A complete List of Tables therefore requires titling 76 tables across 27 manuscripts, out of scope for this batch; a partial list (the ~40 titled ones) would itself be a navigation defect. Also note the finding undercounts: the book has 76 numbered tables, not ~15. Recommend a dedicated build feature (float-based \listoftables or a generated table index) in a follow-up batch.

Not a defect: the LoF difference is the deliberate short-caption mechanism. preface.tex line 118 uses '\caption[The architect's decision loop --- the book's spine]{<full caption>}'; the bracketed optional argument is the standard LaTeX navigation title used by \listoffigures, and render/latex/md_to_latex.py documents this as the intended design (derive_short_caption, 'short title is navigation only'). The full caption appears with the figure in the text, as the book intends. Removing the short captions would put multi-sentence captions into the LoF.

(2) Standardising the title to 'AI SYSTEMS ARCHITECTURE HANDBOOK' without letter-spacing would contradict the approved cover design - the tracked two-line masthead is deliberate typography, and page 3's title page is a different element (serif wordmark + subtitle), not a second rendering that must match glyph-for-glyph. (3) The one real typographic point - no word boundary in the masthead - is fixed under S1 (NBSP word space). No further change made.
